No, family history is not reliable to choose which school children to screen for cholesterol. 

The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends universal cholesterol screening for all children between the ages of 9 and 11, and again between 17 and 21, regardless of family history. This is because many children with high cholesterol do not have a known family history of the condition, and relying solely on family history may miss many cases. Additionally, family history may not be accurately reported or known, particularly in cases of adoption or incomplete family medical history. Universal screening helps to identify all children with high cholesterol, allowing for early intervention and prevention of future cardiovascular disease.
